newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL shares end quieter on mild profit taking.
newsitem.headline: KL shares end quieter on mild profit taking.

text.p: Malaysian equities ended on a quieter note than recent trading sessions, as investors decided to lock in some profits, dealers and analysts said.
The blue-chips Composite Index ended the day down 1.59 points to 1174.01, while the more volatile Second Board index was down 7.13 at 617.52.
"There has been some European buying of blue-chips today, with Malaysian Airlines and Tenaga being unexpectedly strong," said a dealer at a local stock brokerage house.
Traded volume stood at 305 million shares, valued at 2.61 billion ringgit.
"There has been no follow through buying from Friday's activity today," said Faez Khairuddin, head of research of SJ Securities.

On the Kuala Lumpur Options and Financial Futures Exchange the spot October contract was up 2.2 at 1178.5, the November contract was up 0.5 points at 1182.0, while the December contract ended 9.3 points higher at 1188.5. Volumes for the three contracts were 346, 17 and two respectively.
